description: Snowflake's data-type vocabulary is mostly ALIASES onto a handful of real types, measured through INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS as DATA_TYPE/precision/scale/char-length shapes (absent numbers rendered '-'): NUMBER synonyms (DECIMAL/NUMERIC/DEC) keep precision and scale, every integer spelling is NUMBER(38,0) (no narrower range for SMALLINT/TINYINT/BYTEINT), the floating family is FLOAT without precision, varying character spellings default to 16777216 and the fixed three to length 1 (X VARYING is a VARCHAR whatever the head spelling), run-together timestamp spellings are the zoned types (TIMESTAMP WITH LOCAL TIME ZONE is LTZ not TIME), VARBINARY is BINARY. The values too, not just metadata: NUMBER-synonym columns and casts keep declared scale in arithmetic renders (2.500 / 1.5000, stringified so normalization cannot mask them), integer-alias casts round half away from zero, character-synonym casts are identity, the alias spellings stay usable as column names, VARYING only follows the fixed-length spellings, and unknown type names are rejected. Converted 1:1 from features/DataTypeAliasTest (now retired).

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE t_num (c_number NUMBER, c_number_ps NUMBER(7,3), c_decimal DECIMAL, c_decimal_ps DECIMAL(7,3), c_numeric NUMERIC, c_numeric_ps NUMERIC(7,3), c_dec DEC, c_dec_ps DEC(7,3))

SELECT COLUMN_NAME, DATA_TYPE || '/' || COALESCE(TO_VARCHAR(NUMERIC_PRECISION), '-') || '/' || COALESCE(TO_VARCHAR(NUMERIC_SCALE), '-') || '/' || COALESCE(TO_VARCHAR(CHARACTER_MAXIMUM_LENGTH), '-') FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS WHERE TABLE_NAME = 'T_NUM' ORDER BY COLUMN_NAME
CREATE TABLE t_int (c_int INT, c_integer INTEGER, c_bigint BIGINT, c_smallint SMALLINT, c_tinyint TINYINT, c_byteint BYTEINT)

SELECT COLUMN_NAME, DATA_TYPE || '/' || COALESCE(TO_VARCHAR(NUMERIC_PRECISION), '-') || '/' || COALESCE(TO_VARCHAR(NUMERIC_SCALE), '-') || '/' || COALESCE(TO_VARCHAR(CHARACTER_MAXIMUM_LENGTH), '-') FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS WHERE TABLE_NAME = 'T_INT' ORDER BY COLUMN_NAME
CREATE TABLE t_flt (c_float FLOAT, c_float4 FLOAT4, c_float8 FLOAT8, c_double DOUBLE, c_double_p DOUBLE PRECISION, c_real REAL)

SELECT COLUMN_NAME, DATA_TYPE || '/' || COALESCE(TO_VARCHAR(NUMERIC_PRECISION), '-') || '/' || COALESCE(TO_VARCHAR(NUMERIC_SCALE), '-') || '/' || COALESCE(TO_VARCHAR(CHARACTER_MAXIMUM_LENGTH), '-') FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS WHERE TABLE_NAME = 'T_FLT' ORDER BY COLUMN_NAME

CREATE TABLE t_var (c_varchar VARCHAR, c_varchar_n VARCHAR(10), c_string STRING, c_text TEXT, c_nvarchar NVARCHAR, c_nvarchar_n NVARCHAR(10), c_nvarchar2_n NVARCHAR2(10), c_char_v CHAR VARYING, c_char_v_n CHAR VARYING(10), c_character_v_n CHARACTER VARYING(10), c_nchar_v_n NCHAR VARYING(10))

SELECT COLUMN_NAME, DATA_TYPE || '/' || COALESCE(TO_VARCHAR(NUMERIC_PRECISION), '-') || '/' || COALESCE(TO_VARCHAR(NUMERIC_SCALE), '-') || '/' || COALESCE(TO_VARCHAR(CHARACTER_MAXIMUM_LENGTH), '-') FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS WHERE TABLE_NAME = 'T_VAR' ORDER BY COLUMN_NAME
CREATE TABLE t_fix (c_char CHAR, c_char_n CHAR(10), c_character CHARACTER, c_character_n CHARACTER(10), c_nchar NCHAR, c_nchar_n NCHAR(10))

SELECT COLUMN_NAME, DATA_TYPE || '/' || COALESCE(TO_VARCHAR(NUMERIC_PRECISION), '-') || '/' || COALESCE(TO_VARCHAR(NUMERIC_SCALE), '-') || '/' || COALESCE(TO_VARCHAR(CHARACTER_MAXIMUM_LENGTH), '-') FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS WHERE TABLE_NAME = 'T_FIX' ORDER BY COLUMN_NAME

CREATE TABLE t_ts (c_timestamp TIMESTAMP, c_datetime DATETIME, c_ts_ltz TIMESTAMP_LTZ, c_tsltz TIMESTAMPLTZ, c_ts_tz TIMESTAMP_TZ, c_tstz TIMESTAMPTZ, c_tsntz TIMESTAMPNTZ, c_ts_local TIMESTAMP WITH LOCAL TIME ZONE, c_varbinary VARBINARY)

SELECT COLUMN_NAME, DATA_TYPE || '/' || COALESCE(TO_VARCHAR(NUMERIC_PRECISION), '-') || '/' || COALESCE(TO_VARCHAR(NUMERIC_SCALE), '-') || '/' || COALESCE(TO_VARCHAR(CHARACTER_MAXIMUM_LENGTH), '-') FROM INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS WHERE TABLE_NAME = 'T_TS' ORDER BY COLUMN_NAME
CREATE TABLE t_scale (a NUMERIC(7,3), b NUMBER(7,3), c DECIMAL(7,3), d DEC(7,3))
